variants.title: Compact guided form
variants.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE high-fidelity desktop application screenshot mockup refining the attached "03 Guided steps" design.
The input is the design reference and edit target. Retain its app identity, dimmed dark-blue EGT GDA Sync sidebar/header, white dialog, indigo #4b49ac accents, neutral text, crisp realistic UI typography, restrained thin borders, and fixed-size modal with a close X. Redesign the popup according to the variant below. Do NOT reproduce the reference unchanged.
Landscape canvas about 1440x1000, straight-on, no perspective, no device frame, no watermark, no labels outside the app. Keep the full centered modal and fixed footer entirely inside the canvas. Every variant is a TWO-STEP FLOW: "1 Choose destination" active and "2 Review changes" inactive. Show the first step, not a complete reference diff. Main action "Review changes", secondary action "Cancel". The modal does not change size between steps; the body can scroll internally.
Preserve these requirements: Linux-style clickable slash-separated folder path; a compact "Choose subfolder" dropdown immediately after the last folder in that same path row; NO Up button; the filename is already filled in and editable; manual path entry is a quiet disclosure, not another prominent competing input; concise destination preview; assurance of automatic backup. Avoid redundant sections, repeated large path strings, nested pale boxes, decorative illustrations, enormous blank fields, technical hashes, long absolute computer paths, and showing every reference change before the review step.
Identical example content: title "Move asset"; "Topper_JR.dds · 2.0 MB"; source "../joker_reels_coins_10/art/1920x1080/08.Topper/Topper_JR.dds" (may elegantly truncate its middle); source context "From another game", with clear short note "The original file will be kept."; destination "Game folder / art / 1920x1080 / 08.Topper /" followed by the compact subfolder dropdown. The editable field is labelled "File name" and contains "Topper_JR.dds". Destination preview "art/1920x1080/08.Topper/Topper_JR.dds". Show a restrained count "1 file · 2 references". Fixed footer reassurance "A backup is saved automatically." Use clean spelling, generous but controlled spacing, and production-quality implementable layout.
VARIANT 04 — COMPACT GUIDED FORM.
Stay closest to the original guided design but make it more efficient and less boxed. Use a slim horizontal two-step progress line directly below the modal header, with small numbered circles rather than oversized circles. Put the source in one compact muted row with a file icon, a tiny "Copy" badge, the relative source path, and the original-kept note beneath.
Below, a single central form in a comfortably readable column, without full-width pale panels: clear "Destination" heading; one clean address bar with the slash breadcrumbs and inline dropdown; subtle "Enter path manually" link. Then a prefilled filename field below. Finish with a concise destination confirmation row, a small folder icon and the short final relative path, not a large preview card. A thin divider precedes a low-emphasis "Next: review 1 file and 2 references" line. Preserve the exact step-1 flow and fixed footer actions. Plenty of readable white space, but avoid enormous gaps or many dividing lines. This is the clean, practical, quickest-to-scan refinement of the reference, with a smaller visual hierarchy and little chrome.

VARIANT 05 — GUIDED FOLDER EXPLORER.
Retain a horizontal two-step header and all first-step guidance. Give destination browsing the majority of the body. Source is only a thin context strip below the stepper. Beneath the "Destination" heading show the required slash breadcrumb/address row and dropdown. Under it, integrate a compact folder explorer about 250px high: a narrow left tree with Game folder, art, 1920x1080 expanded and 08.Topper selected in pale indigo, alongside sibling folders 01.MainGame, 02.ReelSymbols, 03.Splash. On the right show a clean child-folder area titled "Inside 08.Topper" with two tasteful folder rows "DDS" and "PNG". This is a folder-only picker, not an asset gallery. Keep folder names readable, small line icons, restrained row separators. No Up button or second redundant breadcrumb.
Below the explorer, place "File name" with its prefilled editable input and a short destination confirmation in a tidy horizontal arrangement. A small "1 file · 2 references will be reviewed next" status is secondary. No reference diff panels, no Apply button at this stage. Fixed footer with Cancel and Review changes. The result should feel like a native file chooser embedded naturally into a guided workflow, distinctly more navigational than the compact-form variant.

VARIANT 06 — VERTICAL GUIDED SIDEBAR.
Move the two-step progress navigation into a slim LEFT RAIL inside the modal, approximately 190px wide, with a very light cool-gray background and a vertical connector: "1 Choose destination" highlighted in indigo, "2 Review changes" muted below. Do not also repeat a horizontal stepper. The modal's main top header still reads Move asset with filename/size and the close icon.
The main content to the right remains one quiet column with strong alignment. Its top is a concise source summary, "From another game" with short relative source path and original-kept note. Next, "Destination" with the required slash path and inline subfolder dropdown; quiet manual-entry disclosure under it. Next is the prefilled "File name" input with minimal prefix/suffix help. A thin divider introduces a clean final-location confirmation and the small count "1 file · 2 references". The left rail can contain a small contextual hint near its bottom, but no additional operation steps or technical details.
Use flat surfaces, restrained borders, readable typography and an intentional guided-panel structure. No folder tree, no reference preview sidebar, no large nested cards. Fixed footer across the modal: backup reassurance left, Cancel and Review changes right. This should feel like a polished native desktop wizard with clear spatial orientation and stable dimensions, distinct from both horizontal-stepper variants.
